explanations.f707cec4-iterative_refinement-d1: A prompt needs testing across varied inputs to show where it works and where it fails. Revising based on those results is the core of iterative refinement.
explanations.f707cec4-prompt_structure-d1: The instruction states the task, such as summarize or translate. The other parts supply information or shape the reply but do not name the task.
explanations.f707cec4-context_window-d1: The model only sees the text inside the current request's context window. Earlier chats are not available unless they are included again.
explanations.f707cec4-few_shot_examples-d1: Examples demonstrate the output pattern, so labeled examples in the exact format teach the model what to return.
explanations.f707cec4-language_model_basics-d1: A language model generates text by predicting which text is likely to come next, based on the input it receives and patterns learned in training.
explanations.f707cec4-hallucination_checking-d1: Confident wording does not indicate accuracy, so claims need checking against reliable sources.
explanations.f707cec4-output_formatting-d1: Fixed structure lets code extract values directly. Format determines whether output can be used by software.
explanations.f707cec4-sampling_temperature-d1: Low temperature concentrates sampling on the highest-probability words, so outputs become more predictable. It does not change accuracy or the model's knowledge.
explanations.f707cec4-role_prompting-d1: A role changes the style, focus and perspective of the same model. It does not add knowledge the model already lacks, and the task still has to be stated.
explanations.f707cec4-clear_instructions-d1: A specific format and count tells the model exactly what output to produce, so it does not have to guess.

lesson.explanation: Here is the key idea: a context window is the fixed amount of text a model can consider in one request, like its working memory. Many learners believe the model remembers every past chat, but that is wrong. It only sees the text inside the current context window, so anything outside it is invisible to the model. Compare the right idea with the wrong belief. Right idea: if an earlier detail is not included in the current request, the model cannot use it. Wrong belief: the model keeps a full record of all past conversations and recalls them automatically. This breaks because the model does not store your chats in a running memory; each request is judged only on the text it receives. When a conversation or document exceeds the window, earlier parts drop out and the model can forget details from the start of the exchange. To fix this, restate important facts in your prompt or keep key material within the limit. Check yourself: if a fact from ten messages ago is missing from your latest request, should you expect the model to know it?

resources.title: What is a context window? | IBM
resources.snippet: An LLM’s context window can be thought of as the equivalent of its working memory. It determines how long of a conversation it can carry out without forgetting details from earlier in the exchange. It also determines the maximum size of documents or code samples that it can process at once. questions.prompt: A 500-word English paragraph uses more than 500 tokens in a model's context window. Why?
options: Tokens are often shorter than words, so one word can span several
The window also stores a saved copy of the words
Tokens are counted per sentence rather than per word
Each word is counted twice in the window

questions.prompt: You need a model to analyze a 60-page report, but the chat's context window is too small to hold all of it. What is the best approach?
options: Assume the first pages stay visible while the rest is dropped
Count pages as words and assume the report fits
Expect the model to recall the report from last week's chat
Split the report and send the key sections that fit the window

questions.prompt: A support bot answers a customer's question correctly on day one. On day two, in a new session with no earlier text, it ignores the order number the customer gave on day one. What is the most likely cause?
options: The day-one text is no longer in the context window
The order number used more words than the bot's limit
Earlier messages stay in view but were misread
The bot saved the order number in permanent memory and forgot it
